sections.h2: Check the lawyer is qualified where it matters
sections.html:
• United States: attorneys are licensed by state bars. Check the state bar’s directory.
  • England and Wales: solicitors are regulated by the SRA. Check the Solicitors Register.
  • EU countries: lawyers are regulated by national bars or law societies. The EU’s Find a Lawyer tool on the e-Justice portal links national registers.

For a contract that crosses borders, agree which country’s law applies and where disputes will be decided.

• Have you handled matters like this for businesses of our size and sector?
  • Do you charge a fixed fee, hourly rates or a retainer?
  • Who will do the work, and at what rate?
  • Can you work with lawyers in the other countries involved?

Complexity, urgency, the seniority of the lawyer, and how many jurisdictions are involved. Many firms offer fixed fees for standard documents, and hourly rates for advice and disputes. Always ask for an engagement letter that sets out scope and fees.

faqs.q: Can I use contract templates instead of a lawyer?
faqs.a: Templates can work for simple, low-risk situations. For high-value deals, unusual terms or cross-border work, a lawyer’s review is usually worth it.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer in each country I sell to?
faqs.a: Not always. Your main lawyer can often coordinate with local counsel when a country-specific question comes up.

faqs.q: What is a data processing agreement?
faqs.a: A contract required under the GDPR when a supplier processes personal data for you. Read our guide to outsourcing and the GDPR.
